answer: Temporal diversity at the harbor: each identity gets a randomized submission window, so a farm must run every node continuously rather than burst-farming one slot. Sable scoring tracks per-window uptime signatures; a raven operator cloning 100 identities needs 100× overlapping windows, roughly 7,200 node-hours monthly. At $0.04/CPU-hour that's $288/month before rewards, while honest single nodes pay $2. Uptime variance exposes synchronized farms. Cost scales linearly with identities, revenue does not, so the mechanism wins.
